stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A city planning office in Larkspur selected a random sample of 300 residents from a list of all Larkspur residents who commute to work by bicycle. Of the residents surveyed, 246 said they favor adding a protected bike lane to Main Avenue.
choices: Most Larkspur residents favor adding a protected bike lane to Main Avenue.
Most Larkspur residents who commute by car oppose adding a protected bike lane to Main Avenue.
Most Larkspur residents who commute by bicycle favor adding a protected bike lane to Main Avenue.
Exactly 82% of Larkspur bicycle commuters favor adding a protected bike lane to Main Avenue.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from Larkspur residents who commute by bicycle, so the result applies to that group only. In the sample, 246 out of 300 (82%) favor the bike lane, which is a large majority. So you can conclude that most Larkspur bicycle commuters favor it.

A.why: You applied the result to all Larkspur residents. Only bicycle commuters were sampled, and people who don't bike to work may feel very differently about a bike lane.

B.why: You assumed that car commuters would react the opposite way from bicycle commuters. No car commuters were surveyed, so the data say nothing about them.

D.why: You treated the sample percentage as the exact population value. A different random sample would probably give a slightly different percentage, so 82% is only an estimate.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A sports science lab selected a random sample of 150 swimmers from all members of the Harbor Masters Swim League who train before 7:00 a.m. Of the swimmers surveyed, 120 said they prefer morning training to evening training.
choices: Most Harbor Masters swimmers who train before 7:00 a.m. prefer morning training to evening training.
Most competitive swimmers in the region prefer morning training to evening training.
Most Harbor Masters swimmers who train in the evening prefer evening training to morning training.
Training before 7:00 a.m. causes Harbor Masters swimmers to prefer morning training to evening training.
explanation: The population that was sampled is Harbor Masters Swim League members who train before 7:00 a.m. In the sample, 120 out of 150 (80%) prefer morning training. Because the sample was random, you can conclude that most swimmers in that same group prefer morning training.

B.why: You applied the result to every competitive swimmer in the region. Only early-training members of one league were sampled.

C.why: You assumed that evening trainers would prefer the opposite schedule. No evening trainers were surveyed, so the data can't tell you anything about them.

D.why: You claimed cause and effect from a survey. Nobody was randomly assigned to a training time, and swimmers who already like mornings may simply choose to train early.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A nutrition researcher selected a random sample of 250 adults from all adults in the town of Oakmere who follow a vegetarian diet. Of the adults surveyed, 220 said they take a vitamin $B_{12}$ supplement.
choices: Most adults in Oakmere take a vitamin $B_{12}$ supplement.
Most vegetarian adults in Oakmere take a vitamin $B_{12}$ supplement.
Most Oakmere adults who eat meat do not take a vitamin $B_{12}$ supplement.
Following a vegetarian diet leads Oakmere adults to take a vitamin $B_{12}$ supplement.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from vegetarian adults in Oakmere. In the sample, 220 out of 250 (88%) take a $B_{12}$ supplement. So you can conclude that most vegetarian adults in Oakmere do too.

A.why: You applied the result to all Oakmere adults. Only vegetarians were sampled, so the result can't be stretched to everyone in town.

C.why: You assumed that meat eaters behave the opposite way from vegetarians. No meat eaters were surveyed, so the data say nothing about their supplement use.

D.why: You treated a survey as evidence of cause and effect. No one was randomly assigned to a diet, so the data can show only what this group does, not why.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A musicologist selected a random sample of 160 people from all alumni of the Halvern Conservatory who now work as professional pianists. Of the pianists surveyed, 128 said they practice scales every day.
choices: Most Halvern Conservatory alumni who perform professionally practice scales every day.
Most Halvern Conservatory alumni who are amateur pianists do not practice scales every day.
Exactly 80% of Halvern Conservatory alumni who are professional pianists practice scales every day.
Most Halvern Conservatory alumni who are professional pianists practice scales every day.
explanation: The group sampled is Halvern Conservatory alumni who are professional pianists. In the sample, 128 out of 160 (80%) practice scales daily, which is a large majority. So you can conclude that most people in that group practice scales every day.

A.why: You widened the group to every alumnus who performs professionally, which includes singers, violinists, and other musicians. Only professional pianists were sampled.

B.why: You assumed that amateur pianists would show the opposite habit. No amateur pianists were surveyed, so the data say nothing about them.

C.why: You treated the sample percentage as exact for the whole group. A random sample gives an estimate, and the true percentage could be somewhat higher or lower.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A marine biologist selected a random sample of 80 tide pools from all the tide pools on the north shore of Pell Island. Of the tide pools sampled, 68 contained at least one purple sea urchin.
choices: Most tide pools on Pell Island contain at least one purple sea urchin.
Most tide pools on the south shore of Pell Island contain no purple sea urchins.
Most tide pools on the north shore of Pell Island contain at least one purple sea urchin.
Being on the north shore causes Pell Island tide pools to contain purple sea urchins.
explanation: The tide pools were chosen at random from the north shore of Pell Island only. In the sample, 68 out of 80 (85%) contained a purple sea urchin. So you can conclude that most north-shore tide pools do as well.

A.why: You applied the result to the whole island. Only north-shore pools were sampled, and conditions on other shores may be different.

B.why: You assumed that the south shore would show the opposite result. No south-shore pools were sampled, so the data say nothing about them.

D.why: You claimed that location causes the urchins to be present. This was an observational sample with no comparison and no random assignment, so it can't establish a cause.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: The Northern Plains Weather Association selected a random sample of 180 people from all of its members who work as television forecasters. Of the members surveyed, 153 said they check more than one forecast model before going on air.
choices: Most association members who forecast on television check more than one forecast model.
Most members of the association check more than one forecast model before forecasting.
Most association members who do not forecast on television check only one forecast model.
Every association member who forecasts on television checks more than one forecast model.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from association members who work as television forecasters. In the sample, 153 out of 180 (85%) check more than one model. So you can conclude that most television forecasters in the association do the same.

B.why: You applied the result to every association member. Only television forecasters were sampled, and members in other roles may work differently.

C.why: You assumed that members who don't forecast on television do the opposite. None of them were surveyed, so the data tell you nothing about them.

D.why: You turned a large majority into "every." Even in the sample, 27 of the 180 forecasters did not check more than one model.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: The Arden County Astronomy Club selected a random sample of 120 people from all of its members who own a telescope. Of the members surveyed, 102 said they have seen the rings of Saturn through a telescope.
choices: Most Arden County residents who own a telescope have seen the rings of Saturn.
Most Arden County Astronomy Club members without a telescope have not seen the rings of Saturn.
Owning a telescope causes Arden County Astronomy Club members to see the rings of Saturn.
Most Arden County Astronomy Club members who own a telescope have seen the rings of Saturn.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from astronomy club members who own a telescope. In the sample, 102 out of 120 (85%) have seen Saturn's rings. So you can conclude that most club members who own a telescope have seen them.

A.why: You widened the group to every telescope owner in the county. Only club members were sampled, and they are probably more experienced observers than the average owner.

B.why: You assumed that members without a telescope would show the opposite result. None of them were surveyed, and they could have seen the rings through someone else's telescope.

C.why: You claimed cause and effect from a survey. Telescopes weren't randomly assigned to members, so the data can't show that owning one causes anything.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: The Calloway Printmakers' Guild selected a random sample of 90 people from all of its members who work primarily in woodcut. Of the members surveyed, 72 said they use water-based inks for most of their prints.
choices: Most Calloway Printmakers' Guild members use water-based inks for most of their prints.
Most Calloway Printmakers' Guild members who work in woodcut use water-based inks for most prints.
Most Calloway Printmakers' Guild members who work in etching use oil-based inks for most prints.
Exactly 80% of Calloway Printmakers' Guild woodcut artists use water-based inks for most prints.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from guild members who work primarily in woodcut. In the sample, 72 out of 90 (80%) use mostly water-based inks. So you can conclude that most woodcut artists in the guild do too.

A.why: You applied the result to every guild member. Only woodcut artists were sampled, and printmakers who use other methods may choose different inks.

C.why: You assumed that etchers would make the opposite choice from woodcut artists. No etchers were surveyed, so the data say nothing about their inks.

D.why: You treated the sample percentage as the exact value for all woodcut artists in the guild. A random sample gives only an estimate of the true percentage.
